findings.fix: New check type `boilerplate_stripped` (src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:253). It derives the stripped view and asserts (a) removed == sum(end-start) over the spans -- the assertion a no-op fails first, and the one that also catches removing too much; (b) an optional exact `removed_chars`; (c) an optional `not_contains` list; (d) the reconstruction identity -- stripping a chrome run's OWN window yields '' while normalized_text[start:end] still returns its original characters, which is the `start`/`end` path a caller uses for one item's body. Wired into boilerplate-chrome-detected (removed_chars 2002) and the new boilerplate-section-heads (span-equality only, since jpm's character count is not what that case pins).
findings.verified_red_after_fix: Same no-op mutation, after the fix: fast 73/75 = 0.973, REGRESSION vs baseline 1.000. boilerplate-chrome-detected -> 'stripped view removed 0 chars, spans total 2002'; boilerplate-section-heads -> 'stripped view removed 0 chars, spans total 11388'.

findings.note_on_the_MAX_GAP_CV_half: The finding's evidence also observes that MAX_GAP_CV 0.60 -> 0.80 leaves everything green. Measured after this repair, that is true and is NOT a coverage hole: raising the CV gate to anything below 0.84 changes zero spans on msft-2013, cvx-2015, ge-1994 and jpm-2024, so there is no behaviour difference for a case to detect. 0.84 is the first value that admits a false positive (cvx-2015 gains 17 spans), and boilerplate-near-miss goes red at exactly 0.84. Recorded as a comment on the constant (src/sec10k/boilerplate.py:47-51) so the observation is not re-derived as a defect.

unverified: The CI change itself was not executed on GitHub Actions -- no runner is reachable from this branch. What was verified is the exact command list the unit-tests job declares, run locally, with and without the PAGE_DIGITS mutation.

evals/heldout/ was not run and not looked at, unchanged from the original S6 report: thresholds are implementation and the burn rule forbids tuning them there. The new jpm-2024 case does not change that.

boilerplate-section-heads pins MIN_SPREAD from below (0.40 is red). It does not pin it from above: raising MIN_SPREAD loses recall rather than gaining false positives, and no case asserts a running head that a HIGHER spread gate would drop. MIN_REPEATS is in the same position -- 8 -> 20 is caught only by _demo, which is now in CI (R1), but by no eval case.
